brief: US headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m vs 0.3% expected and core CPI also beat at 0.3%, putting core at about 2.7% y/y, a broad report. Fed's Waller framed this partly as second-round effects from persistent growth and the Q3 energy spike and signaled openness to a 50bp December hike; RBC thinks 50bp is highly unlikely but now sees consecutive 25bp hikes in December and January as probable, with the path after that depending on energy prices. US short rates price 82bps of hikes to October 2027; RBC stays flat US duration but flags the front end as overshooting and attractive. In Israel, Eisenkot looks more likely to oust Netanyahu and form a government, which RBC says lowers the odds of an Iran reescalation; combined with the Democratic midterm "Blue Wave," RBC sees reduced risk of a Trump-driven kinetic war, which would let energy prices resume falling and benefit European duration (RBC stays modestly long France, Italy, Romania). Equities and credit rebounded this week, led by semis on reassuring CoreWeave results and easing funding concerns; credit positioning has cleaned up and new issuance is well received. Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned over an espionage-linked scandal, wiping over $1tn from Nvidia's market cap, with longer-term fallout still unclear per RBC. RBC also trimmed its short-dollar conviction after hawkish Fed comments.
